title: Song of the Four Seasons (Ki Saw Aiom)
khasi_title: Ki Saw Aiom: Pyrem, Lyiur, Synrai, Tlang
cultural_context: Celebrates the four distinct climatic and agricultural seasons of the Khasi Hills: Ka Pyrem (Spring, with blossoming cherry trees and wild orchids), Ka Lyiur (Monsoon, with majestic thunderstorms and flooding waterfalls), Ka Synrai (Autumn, with golden paddy harvest and festive dances), and U Tlang (Winter, with morning frosts, hearthside storytelling, and archery contests).
lyrics_khasi:
Ka Pyrem ka la wan ryngkat u tiew kulab,
Ki sim ki la rwai ha ki tnat ba jyrngam;
Ka Mariang ka la pynphuh ia la ka sopti,
Ki samla ki la mih ban rep ha madan!

Ka Lyiur ka la wan ryngkat ka slapbah,
Ki pyrthat ki la rih, ki kshaid ki la sawa;
Ki thwei ki la shlei, ki um ki la tuid,
Ka ri lum ka la pyngngad baroh shi lyiur!

Ka Synrai ka la wan ryngkat u kba ksiar,
Ki lyngkha ki la tiew ha ka rong ba sngur;
Ki tymmen ki kmen, ki khunlung ki rkhie,
Ngin lum ia u kba sha ki thiar ba khraw!

U Tlang u la wan ryngkat ka erkyrkha,
Ka thah ka la sop ia ki phlang ha madan;
Ha rympei ngin shong ban sngap ia ka parom,
Ki ksing bad ki sharati kin sawa pat ha pyrem!
lyrics_english:
Springtime has arrived accompanied by wild mountain roses,
The forest birds sing upon verdant leafy boughs;
Mother Nature has arrayed her resplendent mantle,
And the youth step forth to cultivate the fertile fields!

Summer Monsoon has arrived with torrential rains,
The thunder rumbles deep, the waterfalls roar across the cliffs;
The gorges overflow, crystal waters tumble free,
And the mountain land rests cool throughout the wet season!

Autumn has arrived laden with golden ripened paddy,
The terraced fields glow in pure radiant amber hue;
The elders rejoice, the children laugh in delight,
As we gather the harvest into the great ancestral granaries!

Winter has arrived with chilly mountain winds,
White frost carpets the meadow grasses in the dawn;
Beside the hearth fire we gather to hear the ancient lore,
Until drums and sweet flutes resound once more in Spring!

stanzas.title: Ka Pyrem (Spring Renewal)
stanzas.khasi:
Ka Pyrem ka la wan ryngkat u tiew kulab,
Ki sim ki la rwai ha ki tnat ba jyrngam;
Ka Mariang ka la pynphuh ia la ka sopti,
Ki samla ki la mih ban rep ha madan!
stanzas.english: Spring arrives with wild roses; birds sing on green boughs. Nature puts on her blossoms, and youth step forth to plow.

stanzas.title: Ka Lyiur (Summer Monsoon)
stanzas.khasi:
Ka Lyiur ka la wan ryngkat ka slapbah,
Ki pyrthat ki la rih, ki kshaid ki la sawa;
Ki thwei ki la shlei, ki um ki la tuid,
Ka ri lum ka la pyngngad baroh shi lyiur!
stanzas.english: Monsoon brings torrential rains; thunder roars and waterfalls echo. Rivers swell and the highlands stay cool all season.

stanzas.title: Ka Synrai (Autumn Harvest)
stanzas.khasi:
Ka Synrai ka la wan ryngkat u kba ksiar,
Ki lyngkha ki la tiew ha ka rong ba sngur;
Ki tymmen ki kmen, ki khunlung ki rkhie,
Ngin lum ia u kba sha ki thiar ba khraw!
stanzas.english: Autumn brings golden paddy; fields glow in amber beauty. Elders rejoice and children laugh as granaries fill with rice.

stanzas.title: U Tlang (Winter Hearth)
stanzas.khasi:
U Tlang u la wan ryngkat ka erkyrkha,
Ka thah ka la sop ia ki phlang ha madan;
Ha rympei ngin shong ban sngap ia ka parom,
Ki ksing bad ki sharati kin sawa pat ha pyrem!
stanzas.english: Winter brings biting breezes; white frost covers the highland meadows. Around hearth fires we listen to ancient tales until flutes welcome Spring.

vocabulary.aiom: Season, climatic period of the annual astronomical cycle
vocabulary.pyrem: Springtime, season of blossoming and sowing (March to May)
vocabulary.lyiur: Summer monsoon, season of heavy rains (June to August)
vocabulary.synrai: Autumn harvest season, season of golden grain (September to November)
vocabulary.tlang: Winter, season of cold mountain breezes and hearth gatherings (December to February)
vocabulary.thah: Frost, white ice crystals covering morning vegetation
vocabulary.thiar: Traditional woven bamboo granary for storing harvested unhusked rice (kba)
vocabulary.rympei: The sacred three-stone matrilineal kitchen hearth fire
